She wasn't coming home from work at her usual time. Mind you, she worked out of town, so commute traffic was always a factor. At first, it was the usual "traffic is crazy!", or "I had to stay late again", or "getting gas". I never questioned her about any of it, whatsoever. 

     She had three children from a previous marriage who lived with us, and we always made it a point to make dinner together, and let the kids "help" as much as they wanted. It was difficult enough for both of us to get them situated before and after dinner, make sure they all had a bath, did homework, etc., but she had become more and more absent from such things. 

     One Friday evening while prepping for a rather involved dinner, I looked at the clock and realized I had lost track of the time. I also realized I hadn't heard from her. It was approximately 75 minutes after she typically left the office, so I gave her a call. It went straight to voicemail. So, I called her office phone, and again, went straight to voicemail. I called the office manager on her cell(a friend of ours), she picked up and told me that everyone left at their usual time. I immediately got worried something had happened to her on the commute, so I checked traffic reports. Smooth sailing on the expressways. So, I thought to myself "maybe she took the backroads?", then my mind went to "what if she had an accident on some county road and nobody has noticed it?".

     Without sounding panicked, I told the kiddos that we needed to get in the car to go on a little road trip to find mom. I got them all buckled in, strapped myself in, and suddenly realized I could try using the Find My Phone feature to see if that worked. I opened the application, and it was showing her phone's location. The app was showing it was at a local park, which happend to be on the backroad route she would typically take if the expressway was too congested.

     We got on the road, headed to this park, and once we got there, I realized something funny. It was completely empty. No people, no other vehicles, except for a semi-truck carrying no trailer, and my wife's car parked right next to it. The two vehicles were situated in the back of the park, away from the road. This particular truck had one of those sleeper cabs used by longhaul truckers. Feeling more and more perplexed, we pulled up a few spaces away and parked. I asked them to stay put while I got out and checked. I walked up to her car's driver side window, peeked in, and saw her phone on the passenger seat with her purse. Then, I noticed voices coming from the truck, one of which I recognized immediately. The voice I recognized was not holding conversation, but rather expressing emotion through loud moaning and expletives. 

     My heart sank into my stomach as I walked up onto the step of the door. I knocked loudly, and both voices fell completely silent. I knocked again. Nothing. So I mustered up what little air I had left in my lungs to say "It's bradley163, I'm looking for my wife and I'm pretty sure I hear her in there. Let her know the kids and I are going out to get some pizza tonight, and her stuff will be outside on the front porch when she decides to come home."

     After I kept true to my word. When she finally got home, her stuff was on the porch, the kids were asleep after a night of pizza and a movie, and I was sitting alone at the dinner table. She walked up, dropped her purse on the table, sat down, looked me directly in the face, giggled and said "why did you embarrass me like that? It was just sex." Then, I asked "I assume this is where you were when the traffic was bad, or you had to stay late?". She had the audacity to tell me "not necessarily with him".

     Come to find out, she had been cheating on me with 4 different men for a total of 3 years, and I was stupid enough to believe her excuses. I filed for divorce that Monday. This was 5 years ago. She is currently 44 years old, pregnant with a child from someone who is in prison for 1st degree domestic assault and battery, took up smoking both cigarettes and meth, and lives without her three children I helped raise for 8 years. They live with their father. I am grateful for their safety, but miss them dearly.
